schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE MODEL'S KEEPER: the single owner-gated door that fills `intentions-congruency-lab/` with a COPY of every intention+why in the system — `CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/` (the homeless intentions: the roots, concept-pieces, host-seams, spanning ones) PLUS every beside-code `intention+why.json` ANYWHERE in the repo. One source, one file, byte-identical; a homeless intention keeps its own name, a charter is prefixed by the component that owns it (`cairn/librarian` -> `cairn-librarian--intention+why.json`) because a flat folder cannot hold thirty-two files all called `intention+why.json`. The lab is regenerated whole, so a source that disappears takes its copy with it. A pure core (`plan_copies(sources)`) decides names and catches collisions with no disk; a thin file layer (`gather_sources`, `copy_to_lab`) is the today-shape. The single write-door is `copy_to_lab`; nothing else writes the lab, and the store's hand-authored `_charter+why.json` (or anything else `_`-prefixed) is never touched.
why:
The seed claim, from the store's own charter: take this one folder to a bare machine and regrow the system. A folder of the actual intention files satisfies that directly — you read them the way you read them anywhere else, with no reader and no envelope in between.

WHAT THIS REPLACED, AND WHY (Akien, 2026-07-31, unambiguous — 'THE SCRIPT'S JOB IS TO COPY THE INTENTIONS+WHY INTO THAT FOLDER. THAT'S ALL'): the first build compiled every source into ONE artifact, `_model.json`, embedding each source's content in a JSON envelope ordered by git birth date. That file is deleted and does not come back. The envelope was a second shape for the same bytes — a thing that can drift from what it represents, and that needed born-timestamps, verbatim-embedding rules and a `--follow` git call to maintain the illusion that it could not. Copies cannot drift. Every one of those mechanisms went away with the artifact that needed them (Law 1: the resolver is not spent re-deriving what a copy already answers).
invoke: Hand-crank: `python3 -m cairn.intentions_model_compiler.compiler` (copies both trees into `intentions-congruency-lab/`, prints the count and any stale copies removed) or `bin/cmd/compile`. In code: `from cairn.intentions_model_compiler import compiler; compiler.copy_to_lab()` (roots auto-derived from `__file__`; override `commons_root`/`code_root`/`out_dir` in proofs). Pure core, no disk: `compiler.plan_copies(sources)` -> `{lab filename: source path}`. Prove: `python3 cairn/intentions_model_compiler/proofs/test_compiler.py` (exit 0 = green).
node_class: code-seam — the compile-door child (a) of ticket intentions-model-compiler, now also carrying the WRITE GATE child (c): a code-seam script (recompile_gate.sh, git-tracked, proven) poked by a WRITE-THROUGH contract (the skills poke the gate in the same act that changes a source) plus a READ-REFRESH backstop (the reader pokes the gate before consulting the model); the prior FileChanged host hook is retired (superseded — see host_seam). Berths in cairn/ (class-space code); the folder it writes is CairnCommons/intentions-congruency-lab/. Kin to cairn/charter (the projector), cross-referenced not merged.

host_seam.what: the MODEL-FRESHNESS CONTRACT — the sole write-door (compile_to_disk, via recompile_gate.sh) is poked by an EVENT, never by a clock or a resident watcher. Three invocations, no fourth, ALL event-driven, NO daemon: (1) MANUAL — the hand-crank / `cairn compile` (the human's command is the event); (2) WRITE-THROUGH baked into /sorted — the skill pokes the gate right after it files a homeless intention to intentions-not-beside-code/ (the source-write is the event); (3) READ-REFRESH baked into /intent — the CONSUMER pokes the gate before consulting the model (the read is the event): at 'I intend X' the reader refreshes (a ~0.2s deterministic compile) then reads, catching every out-of-band write (a human hand-edit, a charter written outside a skill step) exactly when the model is needed and never on a no-op tick. The gate COMMAND (recompile_gate.sh) is class-space/git and proven; nothing stands running.
host_seam.why_not_incremental: MEASURED 2026-07-23 (Law 3): a full recompile of the whole corpus is 0.20s. So 'update vs rebuild' is a distinction without a difference — the writer pokes the ONE deterministic write-door for a full re-projection; there is NO incremental second write-path, which would break the single-door + determinism invariants (falsifiers 2 + 4). 'We don't rebuild by hand' is honored by the writer poking the cheap full door, not by partial updates.
host_seam.consumer: the model's live consumer now is CC + Akien reading it at 'I intend X' — start in the model: is anything already like this, or in conflict (Law 1, caught at n=1)? The check is JUDGMENT OVER THE WHYS the model carries, not a string-match — so no precomputed conflict-edges are needed and none are kept. The reader owns freshness by REFRESH-ON-READ — the probe-native backstop (the read is the event), restored after a wrong detour through a nightly cron daemon (drift; removed). Write-through keeps the model usually-already-fresh so the read rarely changes anything; the read-refresh guarantees no out-of-band write is ever silently stale, with nothing standing running.
host_seam.apply: the write-through call lives in /sorted and the read-refresh in /intent — both are skill instruction-steps, NO host config and NO daemon. Every trigger is an event (a command, a write, a read), never a clock. The freshness discipline is encoded in the skills, not left to CC to remember (Law 4).
host_seam.verify: after a /sorted that files to intentions-not-beside-code/, confirm intentions-congruency-lab/_model.json regenerated (mtime advanced); after a hand-edit to a source out-of-band, confirm the next /intent poke refreshes it before consulting. No host state to verify — there is no daemon and no crontab. The gate COMMAND itself is proven in git (proofs/test_recompile_gate.py).
host_seam.superseded: the FileChanged host hook (the prior child-c wiring) is RETIRED. MEASURED 2026-07-23 (Law 3): FileChanged did NOT fire on ANY write CC can produce — Write tool, Edit tool (post /hooks reload), or Bash subprocess — falsifying the provenance's birth-claim that it fires 'not only the agent's tool-writes'. It watches for changes from OUTSIDE CC's own operations, so it never caught the common case (CC authoring a charter during a build) and it dies with the CC session. The write-through-in-skills (the semantic writer pokes the door) is the resting mechanism it was standing in for; the wiring in .claude/settings.local.json is removed. The intentions-not-beside-code/ heterogeneous-name problem that stumped the FileChanged matcher DISSOLVES here — /sorted pokes the door name-agnostically.
host_seam.iou: the freshness discipline now lives in the SKILLS, not in CC's memory (Law 4 — a rule that matters is structure, not policy that drifts): /intent refreshes-on-read, /sorted writes-through. The one remaining IOU is the owner-gate emit (the source's OWNER emitting on its own write — the emit-chokepoint state-machine-physics tracks); until it lands, the READ-REFRESH at /intent is the structural backstop that makes any missed eager write-through safe, needing no daemon because the read itself is the event. Named so the stopgap is not mistaken for the resting state.
host_seam.state: CONTRACT RECORDED + APPLIED 2026-07-23. Gate COMMAND proven + sealed (validations/test_recompile_gate.json). Write-through baked into /sorted; read-refresh baked into /intent — the freshness discipline lives in the skills (Law 4), not CC's memory. FileChanged wiring removed from .claude/settings.local.json. NO daemon: a nightly cron was installed then REMOVED as drift (a poll on a no-op tick; the read-refresh probe replaced it).

falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) a copy is not BYTE-IDENTICAL to its source — re-serialised, re-indented, key-reordered, or wrapped in any envelope (the moment the lab holds a second shape for the same bytes, it can drift, which is the whole reason `_model.json` is gone); (2) a source is missed or one is invented — in particular a charter outside `cairn/*/`, which is how 13 of 32 went unseen until it was measured 2026-07-31 (Law 8); (3) a source is deleted and its copy stays standing in the lab (a write-only copier — the easy build — makes the folder a graveyard, Law 7); (4) two sources claim one lab filename and one is silently dropped instead of raising; (5) anything `_`-prefixed in the lab is written or deleted — the store's own `_charter+why.json` is a source, not a copy (Law 6); (6) the lab is written by any door other than `copy_to_lab`, or a hand-edited copy survives a run; (7) it grows its OWN authoring — content in the lab traceable to no source — or its own nightly scanner (that work is the inspector regime's, not this door's).
how_it_learns: Yes — it learns its own reach by construction, and that is now a proof tooth rather than a hope: the reach tooth counts every `intention+why.json` on disk and asserts the gather reached all of them, so the day a charter berths somewhere the walk does not go, the proof reds instead of the folder quietly shrinking. That tooth exists because the failure ALREADY HAPPENED silently — the `cairn/*/` scan reached 19 of 32 for weeks while reporting a healthy count. Its horizon: whether a flat folder of ~40 files stays the right shape as the corpus grows, and whether the `component--` prefix convention holds when a real consumer (a bare-machine regrow, the web_server's intentions view) reads the lab — firmed up when that consumer arrives, not guessed now.
traces_to: Law 1 (the system-scale model is compiled once from structure, not re-derived by each reader — the outer row of the projector recursion)
Law 4 (roots surface first BY PHYSICS — born-timestamp ordering, not a hand-placed special case; the store charter's 'the_roots_surface_first')
Law 6 (exactly one owner gates writes to the compiled view — compile_to_disk is the sole write-door; IOU until the tester import-scans)
Law 7 (the compiled view is never a record of truth — a hand-edit is reverted; the sources are the truth)
Law 8 (a lossless projection a hollow build could not fake — nothing dropped, nothing invented)
Law 3 (the born source was chosen by MEASUREMENT — git --follow, after plain first-add was shown to sink the frame)

Green bare (python3) and under the tester; VALIDATION persisted beside-code at validations/test_compiler.json. The WRITE GATE child (c) carries its OWN proof — proofs/test_recompile_gate.py, three teeth a hollow gate could not pass: it pokes the door (the model appears from sources), it reverts a stale model, and it is non-blocking-but-loud-in-the-record (a failed compile exits 0 yet is logged, never swallowed — Law 7). Green bare and under the tester; VALIDATION at validations/test_recompile_gate.json.
